This, my initial page load, says it all for me.

A lot of what is said is true but overall, it is no longer a very accurate depiction.

As it relates to drivers, for instance, Linux often does a better job than Windows because it supports hardware for a longer time. Which of us has not plugged an old peripheral to a new version of Windows and found out that it is no longer supported with no work-around? With Linux, this is not an issue. Another problem related to drivers is that with Windows, they are often poorly-written and the cause of blue screens. On this MSI laptop, the networking and trackpad drivers were both cited as reasons for a blue screen and funny enough, Linux's built-in drivers support the hardware better than the manufacturer's own.

For software, programs for every imaginable task are generally available. In some cases, they might not be as good as what you can get in Windows or MacOS, but they're also free. Try to find free software in the proprietary operating systems which don't come bundled with ads or malware. That Linux software, which is sometimes admittedly sub-par, at least doesn't mistreat your computer in any way and yes, it will do the job.

As for games, Linux is lacking to a certain extent unless you're only looking to play a few 2D games and big name 3D titles. You won't be seeing Assassin's Creed, Need for Speed or FIFA on Linux... ever, but a few noteworthy titles DO make their way and they play extremely well. Right now, the biggest issue, IMO, is not the lack of titles as much as it is the fact that the existing ones don't run as well in Linux as they do in Windows. Third-parties need to start making use of Vulkan to remedy that situation but, of course, you can't blame developers for targeting an operating system with 90% of the potential customer base over one with about 1% of it.

Either way, in the age of slim laptops with Intel HD GPUs, I don't see why anyone would stick to Windows. Unless you have a powerful machine with an expensive stand-alone GPU and use expensive software to do extraordinary things, Windows gives you no benefit over Linux. After all, let's not forget that Windows' security is an absolute joke no matter what you do. Not only does the company STILL collaborate with the NSA and the CIA, it makes no effort to encrypt anything and, if someone takes your laptop, they can EASILY access your private data. Not so with Linux where encryption is built-in and easy to enable and where malware is nearly impossible to install.
